name: Ziggurats
overview: Scripture reveals that ziggurats, such as those associated with Babylon, symbolize human pride and rebellion against God, exemplified by the attempt to ascend to heaven and exalt oneself above the stars of God (Isaiah 14:13; Jeremiah 51:53). These structures represent idolatry and false worship, which God forbids, commanding His people to destroy the high places and images where pagan nations served their gods (Leviticus 26:1; Deuteronomy 12:2). The downfall of Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, serves as a divine judgment against such arrogance and idolatry (Isaiah 13:19), reminding believers to trust in the Lord alone rather than human efforts to reach or rival heaven.
